title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
conclusions: Introduces residual learning: layers fit a residual mapping F(x) := H(x) - x realized via identity shortcut connections, added back to the stacked-layer output.

Shows very deep plain CNNs suffer a degradation problem (higher training error, not overfitting) as depth increases; residual reformulation makes 18-152 layer nets easy to optimize and gain accuracy with depth on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.

Section 3.4/4.2 documents the standard ImageNet/CIFAR training recipe used for all their models: SGD with momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0001, batch normalization after each conv, standard scale/color/crop augmentation, mini-batch size 256, learning-rate step decay divided by 10 at error plateaus.

152-layer ResNet ensemble achieves 3.57% top-5 error on ImageNet test set, winning 1st place at ILSVRC 2015 classification; also 1st place in ImageNet detection/localization and COCO detection/segmentation via better learned features.
Explores networks over 1000 layers (1202-layer) showing no optimization difficulty but worse test error than the 110-layer network, attributed to overfitting on the small CIFAR-10 dataset.
our_use: main.tex:350, in the Backbones paragraph: "All backbones use standard ImageNet-style training conventions \citep{he2016deep}." Cited as the canonical source for the generic SGD/BN/augmentation/LR-schedule training recipe applied to all three backbones (MobileNetV3, RegNetY-400MF, ViT-B/16), not for the residual-connection architecture itself.
issues: None found in the bibtex fields. The citation itself is a generic/boilerplate convention-citation (He et al. 2016 is used here purely as a stand-in reference for 'standard ImageNet training practice,' not for anything ResNet-specific like residual connections), which is common practice in the literature and does not misrepresent the paper -- Sec. 3.4/4.2 of the paper does explicitly describe exactly that standard SGD+BN+augmentation+step-decay recipe on ImageNet/CIFAR. No overclaim or hallucination detected.
